title: What Makes a Gift Wise?
subtitle: 什麼樣的禮物才算聰明？歐．亨利〈聖誕禮物〉

beginner.title: One Dollar and Eighty-Seven Cents
paras: It is the day before Christmas in New York. A young woman called Della counts her money three times. She has only one dollar and eighty-seven cents. She wants to buy a Christmas present for her husband, Jim, but this is not enough for anything nice. So she sits down on the old couch and cries.
這是紐約聖誕節的前一天。一個名叫黛拉的年輕女子把她的錢數了三遍。她只有一塊八毛七。她想為丈夫吉姆買一份聖誕禮物，但這點錢買不了什麼好東西。於是她坐在舊沙發上哭了起來。

Della and Jim are poor, but they have two treasures. One is Jim’s gold watch, which was his father’s and his grandfather’s. The other is Della’s beautiful long brown hair. Della has an idea. She goes to a shop and sells her hair for twenty dollars.
黛拉和吉姆很窮，但他們有兩樣寶貝。一樣是吉姆的金錶，那是他父親和祖父傳下來的；另一樣是黛拉美麗的棕色長髮。黛拉想到一個辦法。她走進一家店，用二十美元賣掉了她的頭髮。

With the money, she buys a simple chain for Jim’s watch. It costs twenty-one dollars. When Jim comes home, he stares at her short hair. He is not angry. He gives her his present: a set of beautiful combs for her long hair. Della has wanted them for a long time.
她用這筆錢為吉姆的錶買了一條樸素的錶鍊，花了二十一美元。吉姆回到家，盯著她的短髮。他沒有生氣。他把禮物送給她：一組漂亮的梳子，正適合她的長髮。黛拉想要這組梳子已經很久了。
Then Della gives Jim the watch chain. Jim smiles and says that he sold his watch to buy the combs. Now neither of them can use their gift. But they have learned how much they love each other.
接著黛拉把錶鍊送給吉姆。吉姆笑了，說他為了買梳子，把錶賣了。現在兩個人都用不上自己收到的禮物。但他們明白了彼此有多相愛。

This short story is by O. Henry, an American writer famous for surprise endings. It first appeared in a New York newspaper in December 1905. The Magi were the wise men who brought gifts to baby Jesus. At the end, O. Henry says that Della and Jim were the wisest of all. Why? Because they gave the most important thing: themselves.
這篇短篇小說的作者是歐．亨利，一位以出人意料的結局聞名的美國作家。它在 1905 年 12 月首次刊登在紐約的一份報紙上。「麥琪」指的是帶著禮物去看嬰兒耶穌的智者。故事最後，歐．亨利說黛拉和吉姆才是最有智慧的人。為什麼？因為他們送出了最重要的東西：他們自己。

intermediate.title: What Makes a Gift Wise?
paras: “One dollar and eighty-seven cents. That was all.” So begins one of the most famous short stories in American literature. Della Young has counted her savings three times, and the total has not changed. Tomorrow is Christmas, and she has been saving every penny for months to buy her husband, Jim, a present worthy of him. With his income cut to twenty dollars a week, it has not been enough.
「一塊八毛七。就這麼多。」美國文學中最有名的短篇小說之一，就這樣開場。黛拉．楊已經把她的積蓄數了三遍，總數還是沒變。明天就是聖誕節，好幾個月來，她省下每一分錢，就是想為丈夫吉姆買一份配得上他的禮物。但吉姆的收入被砍到一週二十美元，錢還是不夠。

The couple own two possessions they are proud of. One is Jim’s gold watch, passed down from his father and grandfather. The other is Della’s hair, so beautiful that, O. Henry jokes, it would make the Queen of Sheba jealous. In a moment of courage, Della visits a shop run by a Madame Sofronie and sells her hair for twenty dollars. She then spends twenty-one dollars on a platinum chain for Jim’s watch.
這對夫妻擁有兩樣引以為傲的東西。一樣是吉姆的金錶，從他的祖父、父親一路傳下來；另一樣是黛拉的頭髮，歐．亨利開玩笑說，美得足以讓示巴女王嫉妒。黛拉鼓起勇氣，走進一位叫索芙羅妮夫人開的店，以二十美元賣掉了頭髮。接著，她花了二十一美元，為吉姆的錶買了一條白金錶鍊。

When Jim arrives home and sees her short hair, he freezes. Then he hands her a package. Inside are the combs she had admired in a shop window for a long time — perfect for the long hair she no longer has. When Della proudly presents the chain, Jim smiles and explains that he sold his watch to buy the combs. Instead of being upset, he suggests that they put their presents away for a while, and asks Della to start cooking dinner.
吉姆回到家，看見她的短髮，整個人愣住了。接著他遞給她一個包裹。裡面是她在櫥窗前欣賞了很久的梳子——正適合她已經不再擁有的長髮。當黛拉驕傲地拿出錶鍊時，吉姆笑了，解釋說他為了買梳子，把錶賣了。他沒有難過，反而提議先把禮物收起來一陣子，並請黛拉開始煮晚餐。

O. Henry, the pen name of William Sydney Porter, was known for exactly this kind of twist. The story first appeared in The New York Sunday World on 10 December 1905 and was later collected in his book The Four Million. On the surface, the ending seems almost cruel: two sacrifices that cancel each other out, leaving two useless gifts.
歐．亨利是威廉．西德尼．波特的筆名，他正是以這種出人意料的轉折聞名。這篇故事在 1905 年 12 月 10 日首次刊登於《紐約星期日世界報》，後來收錄在他的書《四百萬》中。表面上，這個結局近乎殘酷：兩份犧牲互相抵銷，只留下兩份派不上用場的禮物。

Yet the final paragraph turns the story around. The Magi, O. Henry reminds us, were the wise men who brought gifts to the baby Jesus. Della and Jim might look like “two foolish children” who acted unwisely. But, he insists, of all who give gifts, these two were the wisest. The value of a gift, the story suggests, lies not in what it is worth, but in what the giver was willing to give up.
然而最後一段把整個故事翻轉過來。歐．亨利提醒我們，麥琪是帶著禮物去看嬰兒耶穌的智者。黛拉和吉姆看起來或許像「兩個傻孩子」，做了不明智的事。但他堅持：在所有送禮的人當中，這兩人才是最有智慧的。故事暗示，禮物的價值不在於它值多少錢，而在於送禮的人願意為它放棄什麼。

advanced.title: Foolish Sacrifice, Wise Love
paras: Few short stories are as compact, or as frequently retold, as O. Henry’s “The Gift of the Magi.” First published in The New York Sunday World on 10 December 1905 under the title “Gifts of the Magi,” and later collected in The Four Million, it occupies only a few pages. Yet within that brief space it manages a complete emotional arc and an ending that readers still remember long after they have forgotten its details. According to a popular account, O. Henry wrote it at Pete’s Tavern on Irving Place in New York City, although the claim is difficult to prove.
很少有短篇小說像歐．亨利的〈聖誕禮物〉這樣精簡，又這樣被一再重述。它在 1905 年 12 月 10 日以〈麥琪的禮物們〉為題首次刊登於《紐約星期日世界報》，後來收錄在《四百萬》中，篇幅只有短短幾頁。然而在這麼小的空間裡，它完成了一段完整的情感弧線，以及一個讀者在忘記細節之後仍久久記得的結局。根據一個流傳甚廣的說法，歐．亨利是在紐約歐文街上的皮特酒館寫下這篇故事的，不過這個說法很難證實。

The story opens with a precise and humiliating figure: one dollar and eighty-seven cents, sixty cents of it in pennies saved by bargaining with the grocer and the butcher. Della Young has counted it three times. The details of poverty accumulate — a furnished flat at eight dollars a week, a letter-box into which no letter would fit, an income shrunk from thirty dollars to twenty. O. Henry treats these facts with gentle irony, but he never pretends they do not hurt.
故事以一個精確又令人難堪的數字開場：一塊八毛七，其中六毛是跟雜貨店老闆和肉販討價還價省下來的一分錢銅板。黛拉．楊已經數了三遍。貧窮的細節一層層堆疊——一週八美元的附家具公寓、一個塞不進任何信的信箱、從三十美元縮水到二十美元的收入。歐．亨利以溫和的反諷處理這些事實，但他從不假裝它們不痛。

Against this background stand the couple’s two treasures: Jim’s gold watch, inherited from his father and grandfather, and Della’s hair, which the narrator claims would have made the Queen of Sheba envious. The symmetry is deliberate. Della sells her hair for twenty dollars to buy a platinum watch chain; Jim, unknown to her, sells his watch to buy the tortoise-shell combs she has longed for. Each sacrifice destroys the usefulness of the other’s gift. Della had admired those combs in a Broadway window for a long time, without the least hope of ever owning them; now they are hers, but the hair they were meant for is gone.
在這樣的背景下，出現了這對夫妻的兩樣寶貝：吉姆從祖父和父親繼承來的金錶，以及黛拉的頭髮——敘事者聲稱它能讓示巴女王嫉妒。這種對稱是刻意的。黛拉以二十美元賣掉頭髮，買了一條白金錶鍊；吉姆在她不知情的情況下，賣掉了錶，買下她渴望已久的玳瑁梳子。每一份犧牲，都毀掉了對方禮物的用處。黛拉在百老匯的櫥窗前仰慕那組梳子很久，從不敢奢望擁有；如今梳子是她的了，該配戴它們的長髮卻已不在。

Read purely as plot, the ending is almost absurd, and O. Henry anticipates this objection. He describes his own tale as “the uneventful chronicle of two foolish children” who “most unwisely sacrificed for each other the greatest treasures of their house.” The self-mockery is a rhetorical move: by naming the reader’s likely judgement first, he prepares to overturn it.
如果單純當作情節來讀，這個結局近乎荒謬，而歐．亨利早就料到這種反對意見。他把自己的故事形容為「兩個傻孩子平淡無奇的紀事」，說他們「極不明智地為彼此犧牲了家中最珍貴的寶物」。這種自嘲是一種修辭手法：先把讀者可能的評斷說出口，再準備把它推翻。

The overturning comes in the final lines. The Magi, he reminds us, were wise men who invented the art of giving Christmas presents, and their gifts were no doubt wise ones. Yet of all who give and receive gifts, Della and Jim are the wisest: “They are the magi.” The story thus redefines wisdom itself. A wise gift, in O. Henry’s sense, is not one that is practical or cleverly chosen, but one that reveals how completely the giver is prepared to put another person first. Tellingly, Jim does not mourn his watch. He simply suggests that they put their presents away for a while, and asks Della to put the chops on for dinner.

翻轉出現在最後幾行。他提醒我們，麥琪是發明聖誕送禮藝術的智者，他們的禮物無疑是明智的。然而，在所有送禮與收禮的人當中，黛拉和吉姆才是最有智慧的：「他們就是麥琪。」故事因此重新定義了「智慧」本身。在歐．亨利的意義上，一份明智的禮物，不是實用或挑得巧妙的禮物，而是能顯示送禮者多麼徹底地願意把另一個人放在第一位的禮物。耐人尋味的是，吉姆並沒有為他的錶傷心。他只是提議先把禮物收起來一陣子，並請黛拉把肉排下鍋準備晚餐。
